open_points.subject: M22 SpooledFile / inspect action
open_points.text: "Read by ... the owner inspecting its bytes ... owner only whatever the class, while its run holds its spool" (M22) vs State 0 inspect action "inspect functions, flows, runs, bindings, approvals, standing grants and effect attempts | owner, agent | typed description"
open_points.question: Can an agent ever read spooled file bytes (for non-personal-data files), or are file bytes owner-only in all cases?
options: Agents may read non-personal-data file bytes
Agents never read bytes, only digests/metadata, regardless of class

open_points.subject: M24 EffectApproval.preview
open_points.text: "preview: what the owner saw — ... the built request and the input values; agents may read approvals, and an agent receives personal-data values only as digest and class"
open_points.question: When agents read approvals, does preview include full non-personal values (including large structures/file content references), or only digests/metadata?
options: Full non-personal values are returned to agents
Only digests/classes are returned to agents for all classes
Values are returned but files are always by digest/metadata only
open_points.default_guess: Return full non-personal values, but files by digest/metadata only.

open_points.subject: M28 Installation / owner principal token lifecycle
open_points.text: "owner_token, agent_tokens" (M28 fields) with continuity text "the token list is read again whenever it has changed, so adding or revoking a token takes effect at the agent's next request (K-15)"
open_points.question: Does live token re-read apply only to agent tokens, or also to owner_token changes (rotation/revocation) without restart?
options: Only agent_tokens are hot-reloaded; owner_token changes require restart
Both owner_token and agent_tokens are hot-reloaded
No tokens are hot-reloaded; restart required
open_points.default_guess: Only agent_tokens are hot-reloaded; owner_token changes require restart.

open_points.subject: M19 Run lifecycle (end conditions while waiting)
open_points.text: "The run is `failed` when no node can run any more and some node failed" together with "No wait ends by itself" (K-09) and run statuses including `awaiting_approval`/`pending`
open_points.question: If a run has waiting points (approval/unknown/unreachable) and also has at least one failed branch, does it stay waiting until waits are decided/resolved, or end `failed` immediately once no runnable node exists?
options: Waiting status has precedence; run does not auto-fail while any waiting point exists
Failed status has precedence when no runnable node exists, even if waiting points remain
open_points.default_guess: Waiting status has precedence; do not auto-fail while any waiting point exists.
